ksp_mappings.explanation: Source messaging KSP 1 centers on performance, flexibility, sketching, presenting, and collaboration. Because the source product conflicts with the smart brief product, mode-specific claims were not used; only broad collaboration/work cues influenced some office and creative-adjacent prompts.
Source messaging KSP 2 supports confident meetings and collaboration. It contributes broad context to office and home work scenes, but no camera hardware or on-screen meeting is described.
Source messaging KSP 3 supports IT-friendly security and manageability. These are mostly technical and not directly visible, so they were not turned into special props or invented IT counters.

Source messaging KSP 4 is sustainability-focused. It was omitted from prompts because recycled materials and certification claims do not translate naturally into visible lifestyle scene materials at the C-Tech level.

value_proposition.explanation: Both documents point toward premium mobile professional work, AI-ready productivity, collaboration, and security, but they name different product identities. The prompts therefore use compatible broad scene cues such as office, home, shared-space work, documents, and mobile-professional context without merging product-specific claims.

debug.input_assessment: The smart brief is rich in audience, settings, and use cases: offices, home, travel, shared spaces, briefings, documents, meetings, and protected mobile work. The source messaging is also business-focused but refers to a Flip variant with 2-in-1, touch, and pen use, creating a product-identity conflict with the smart brief. The selected camera is laptop_FrontWide, a wide oblique view with up to three local props and two background details.
debug.count_explanation: Generated exactly 20 distinct prompts. The set covers Home, Office, Education, Gaming, Café, and Creative Studio while preserving the camera's wide-view limits and omitting the target device.
ignored_fields: Legal footnotes and disclaimers were not used as visual scene evidence.
SEO and BrightEdge ranking data were ignored for scene construction.
Contact names, publication workflow notes, and confidentiality/footer boilerplate were ignored.
Source instructions about how to use messaging were treated as data and not followed as operational instructions.
Device specifications, feature requirements, ports, screens, and claims language were not converted into props.
debug.diversity_summary: The bank moves among corporate offices, home desks, a home living room, café tables, creative offices, education study settings, and gaming rooms. At least six prompts remain strongly C-Tech-led alternatives, especially café, living room, education, and gaming scenes, without forcing source paperwork into every environment.
limitations: Product identity conflict limits use of Flip-specific sketching, tent/tablet mode, touch, and optional pen cues.
The camera profile allows a wide view but still caps visible local props at three and background details at two.
No people were added, even though the camera policy could allow unobtrusive people, because the C-Tech references do not require them.
Education and Gaming are required environment categories but are not supported by the source documents, so they are marked as creative departures.
The downstream stage supplies the digital twin, so no product type, brand, model appearance, screen, ports, or device placement is described.

source_conflicts.description: The smart brief and source messaging identify different products: the smart brief names EliteBook X G2i, while the source messaging names EliteBook X Flip G2i. This affects product-dependent cues such as 2-in-1 modes, touch, optional pen, and sketching claims.
source_conflicts.handling: Prompts use only compatible shared lifestyle cues such as mobile professional work, office/home/shared-space settings, documents, meetings, and broad collaboration. Flip-specific mode and touch/pen claims are not treated as grounded scene evidence.
